item.title: Monaghan Gardaí appeal for information on stolen tools
item.description: Detective Gardaí attached to Monaghan and Carrickmacross Garda Station have recovered a large quantity of tools and power tools, that are suspected to be stolen. It comes following an intelligence led operation led by An Garda Síochána. In a post on social media, Detective Gardaí said they wish to identify the owner of these items. item.title: Border farmers urged to watch out for bluetongue
item.description: The Agriculture Minister says his Department is working hard to stop the spread of animal borne diseases. Farmers in border counties are being urged to watch out for bluetongue in cattle after two cases were confirmed in Northern Ireland. A housing order remains in place for poultry after a fifth outbreak of bird flu was confirmed this week. item.title: Emyvale community consultation on N2 border scheme
item.description: A community consultation event will take place today to share the updated designs of the N2 Clontibret to the border scheme. The drop in information clinic will take place at the Emyvale recreation Centre today between 3pm and 8pm. Cllr Niamh McCooey said these meetings are off the back of community and landowner engagements where concerns of the community were listened to. item.title: Changing demographics 'great' for Monaghan Harps
item.description: The Monaghan Harps' GAA Club has highlighted how its demographics have changed in recent years. Una Forde, the club's healthy club officer, said that over the previous 15 years, different nationalities have become involved with the club. Speaking to Northern Sound, she said that children from other countries have began playing with the club for longer. item.description: The attention turns back to the Night Navigation season this Saturday night as the Skibbereen & District Car club host their Carbery trial. item.title: Local 'concern' over adult asylum seekers placed in children’s care
item.description: 192 adult asylum seekers were placed in children’s accommodation over the past three years. Tulsa had mistakenly placed the international protection applicants in children’s care, before establishing they were over 18. This year there have been 86 such cases, that’s more than double the 2023 figures. Advertisement The information was obtained by Cavan-Monaghan TD Matt Carthy. item.title: Smith: 'Urgent need to enact legacy framework'
item.description: The Taoiseach has said he believes that there is a "sincere commitment" on behalf of the British Government on the implementation of the Legacy Framework. Deputy Smith outlined that there is an urgent need to enact legacy legislation to give effect to the provisions outlined in the framework. item.title: National league fixtures are released
item.description: Monaghan will open their Division 1 league campaign when they welcome Armagh to St Tiernachs Park Clones on Sunday January 25th at 2pm. That will be 1 of 4 home games the Farney side will have as Mayo, Galway and Donegal will all be hosted by Gabriel Bannigans side.
